newsitem.title: UK: ICL making substantial investment in BBC Online.
newsitem.headline: ICL making substantial investment in BBC Online.

text.p: Information technology company ICL said on Thursday it was investing several million pounds in a new online venture with the British Broadcasting Corporation.
"There is a substantial investment in infrastructure. It certainly is many millions of pounds," ICL chief executive Keith Todd told a news conference.
ICL, controlled by Japanese giant Fujitsu, and the BBC have joined forces to set up BBC Online, a commercial service that will be available on the Internet from next spring.
The BBC is not permitted to invest public funds in commercial ventures such as BBC Online.
Revenues will be shared between ICL and BBC Worldwide, the BBC's commercial arm.
Todd said that there were plans to run advertising on the service and charge a subscription for premium services.
The web site will be free to anyone who has access to the Internet but there will be a charge for those who opt to use the BBC Online access service developed as part of the project.
In addition to the BBC-branded access service, Internet users will be able to call up the service via exisiting routes such as CompuServe, America Online and Demon and Pipex.

Todd said the inital service would largely be based on text and graphics but BBC Worldwide chief executive Bob Phillis added that the development of audio and visual services could be developed as technology advanced.
